title: Atlantean Citadel
html:
The main entrance room in the Atlantean Citadel interior.

The Atlantean Citadel is an ancient temple themed interior that frequently spawns on Atlantica, Berunah, Hyve, Junic, Roart, and Thalasso. This interior also has a rare chance to spawn on any moon.

> Rooms

  • Vault - A lever can be pulled in the main entrance area to raise up a hidden Vault with symbols on it. Completing a Secondary Objective allows players to interact with the lever on it and open it.
  • Great Hall - A large area with various branching pathways connecting to the rest of the interior that has three floors. It is always connected to the main entrance.
  • Observatory - A room with several tower structures and a starry roof. This room is primarily for the Seek the Hidden Stars objective.
  • Grates - A spiral staircase leading to a grate that can be pushed upward. Players can remain at the top of the staircase and jump to avoid drowning during interior floods.
  • Sunroof - Sunlight can be seen from the roof of a large pit. This doesn't actually lead to the exterior and attempting to reach the top with a jetpack will deal 666 damage to and cut the player in half. There is a staircase players can use to avoid drowning when the interior floods.
  • Tunnels - Tunnels that players must crouch-walk into. Entities can go into these tunnels.

> Interior Features

  • Chests - Chests can be found in the interior that can have scrap in them. This scrap is separate from the rest of the scrap initially generated on a moon and spawns when the chest is opened.
  • The weather slightly alters the appearance of the interior. For example, rain can be seen pouring from the Sunroof during Rainy, Stormy, or Flooded weather.
  • The color of this interior depends on the moon it spawns on.

> Hazards

  • Axe Trap - Sometimes there can be a pressure plate that when stepped on triggers an axe to swing across, dealing 100 damage to any player caught in its path. This can be avoided by moving fast enough or jumping over the pressure plate.
  • Eye Trap - An eye that looks around periodically. Any players that enter its line of sight will anger it, causing it to release spikes from various holes in the room dealing 33 damage. This can be avoided by avoiding its gaze or by running out of the room fast enough after angering it.

> Beholder's Eye

A Beholder's Eye in a hidden treasure chamber.

The Beholder's Eye serves as the apparatus for the interior, and two are guaranteed to spawn on either side of the interior. Both are worth ▮180, are two-handed, and weigh 36lbs. Each one is located behind a special locked door that can only be opened with a "Dungeon key", and two keys are guaranteed to spawn in the interior as scrap.

When the first Beholder's Eye is taken, all other apparatus related events will be triggered and the interior will begin to flood. The player must utilize the Grates, Sunroof, remain on the third floor at the Great Hall, or simply wait outside to avoid drowning. The water level will rise and persist for about 105 seconds before draining in the next 15 seconds, making the whole sequence last for about 120 seconds.

Although water can still be heard gushing in either of the Beholder's Eye rooms, the interior can only flood once a day and the second Beholder's Eye can be safely retrieved provided another key is found.


> Secondary Objectives

The Vault that holds the reward.

One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn in the Vault.

Fill the Waters of Tribute

If the four basins are not lit up on the Vault, players must find a room with four water basins, writing on the walls, and a door similar to the Vault door. Players must follow the instructions written on the wall to press the buttons to pour the exact amount of water needed into each basin. The numbers written use Roman numerals.

If sucessful, the door similar to the Vault door will open to reveal a lever. Interacting with this lever will cause a sound effect to play and players can return to and open the Vault to get their reward.

Turn On the Fountains

If the three fountains are not lit up on the Vault, players must find three fountains in the interior. At least one typically spawns in the Great Hall. They must then interact with five buttons in a random order to turn them on, and the buttons will reset to the starting position if pressed in the wrong order. A sound effect will play and water will begin to flow from the fountain if successful.

Once all three fountains have been turned on, a sound effect will play and players can return to and open the Vault to get their reward.

Seek the Hidden Stars

If the observatory looking at a star is not lit up on the Vault, players must find the Observatory. A tower light will be on and players can interact with a panel in the room to turn it up, down, left, and right. Players must locate the random position of three hidden stars. The light from the observatory will get smaller as players get closer to a star. A red star will form and a jingle will play when a star is successfully found.

After players locate all three hidden stars, a sound effect will play and it will start visually storming in that room. Players can now return to and open the Vault to get their reward.

The reward is randomized, but the chance for a more valuable reward is increased by how early in the day players complete the objective and is influenced by the vanilla luck system. The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. Fill the Waters of Tribute is considered Easy difficulty and has a 1.0x multiplier. Turn On the Fountains and Seek the Hidden Stars are considered Hard difficulty and have a 1.4x multiplier. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section.

> Event: Atlantean Tomb

The Atlantean Tomb after starting the event.

The Atlantean Tomb can randomly generate in the interior. It is a room with a center device and several inactive Eye Traps on the wall. To start the event, players must interact with three levers in a random order on the back of the central device. This will cause the door to the room to shut and the lights to turn on.

Players must now interact with seven levers on the wall in a random and sequential order. Activating the wrong lever will cause all levers to reset. One strategy players can use is to give a number to each lever in their head to make it easier to remember the correct sequence.

While players do this, three different traps can activate. The first trap activates immediately after starting the event, where an Eye Trap reveals itself in the center device and begins spinning towards a player. The speed of its spin depends on how far away it is from a player, and weightless players can outpace it by simply walking in the same direction of the spin. Players can not duck under its line of sight even though it looks possible to do. If it is triggered, several spikes that deal 33 damage each will come out of the center device. Players can stand on the edge of the center device to avoid the attack.

After players have activated two successful levers, the Eye Traps on the wall will begin activating at random. They behave the same as the hazard and activate the spikes around them. The rate at which the Eye Traps activate and how many are active at any given time increases based on the progress made on the correct lever sequence.

After players have successfully activated four levers, a giant eye will periodically become active and reveal itself on the ceiling to look down at the whole room. It will then get angry and cause several blades to shoot from the ground and slowly rotate around a ring near the center. These blades will shortly recede back into the ground and each blade does 33 damage per hit to players on contact. This attack can easily be avoided by going closer to the center.

After players activate all seven levers in the correct order, all the eyes will begin to close and the center device will lower. It will then raise back up to reveal four Golden bones. Each bone is conductive, weighs 16lbs, and is worth ▮112-151.
